title: Renew staff upstream credentials inside the Papyrus grant service
description:
## Intent

Keep an authorized staff connection usable beyond the initial Cognito JWT without creating a second approval or sending upstream credentials to the host. Depends on PPY-c898ac, PPY-cf2ab5 and PPY-ca57a5.

## Steps

1. In the existing private MCP grant Lambda, add a narrow provider adapter. Exchange the upstream authorization code with the configured Cognito token endpoint and original provider PKCE verifier. Reuse the CLI login protocol's Google/Cognito primitives or contracts where they fit. Keep the CLI loopback/device broker, workstation keyring and browser refresh token out of the hosted flow. Store each connection's own upstream token family, encrypted, and never disclose it in a verify response except for the minimum fresh ID token needed by the private staff tool handler.
2. Verify issuer, exact app client, token use, nonce on initial ID token, matching subject/auth_time, expiry, and applicable site role on issuance and refresh. Bind the first successful Cognito exchange to its original provider refresh deadline and record it once. Use the configured seven-day upstream policy only for the reviewed client. On reconnect after hard expiry, require provider reauthentication and confirm a fresh signed auth_time before granting another window. A provider deployment that cannot prove freshness remains on short grants.
3. Renew upstream only when the current downstream JWT cannot cover the next access-token window or after it expires. Acquire a conditional per-grant in-flight reservation with a fencing version before calling Cognito. A concurrent valid attempt gets a retryable service response while the reservation is active. Do not call Cognito twice with the same rotating secret. A revoke can move the grant to revoked during the reservation. A late provider response cannot re-open it.
4. Use Cognito OAuth refresh against the same configured client with rotation and zero grace. On success, verify the replacement pair and atomically commit the encrypted replacement credentials, spent MCP refresh hash and replacement host pair using the same fenced version. A documented provider failure that did not consume the credential can clear the reservation and return 503; invalid_grant, a lost provider response, an expired reservation or confirmed provider success without durable storage fail closed and require reconnect. Where possible revoke an orphaned provider token. Never retry an editorial write as part of auth recovery.
5. At discovery, refresh and protected calls, use the verified subject's current publication permissions. For renewable staff, use the managed grant service role for site-pool-only read of enabled status and current groups, compare the signed Cognito username and subject, and fail closed on removal or mismatch. A backend outage is 503 and must not elevate or convert the caller. Keep Account and record isolation and existing tool permission checks downstream. For same-origin readers, prove a per-request Prospectus current identity check against the original site subject. Evaluate the existing currentPerson route with the short-lived, encrypted server-held access token and prove it detects removal or subject change. A confirmed denial revokes the connection. An unavailable check returns 503. Keep reader MCP closed where authoritative current eligibility cannot be verified. Preserve Reader Steering availability rules and the shorter Prospectus deadline. Do not broaden scoped tools in shared backends.

## Gherkin acceptance

Feature: Renew a connected staff identity
Scenario: The original staff JWT expires during a grant
  Given the connection is within its fixed deadline and the editor still has access
  When the host refreshes
  Then Papyrus uses a fresh JWT for the same verified editor
  And the host receives only the replacement MCP pair

Scenario: Provider rotation succeeds without a confirmed local commit
  Given a renewal was reserved and the provider outcome is ambiguous
  When another request tries to use the connection
  Then the service cannot mint another pair or run a tool
  And the member must reconnect

Scenario: The editor is disabled or loses the required role
  Given a formerly authorized connection still has an unexpired bearer token
  When the host attempts a protected operation
  Then the operation is refused without changing data
  And restoring the role does not reactivate a revoked grant

## Verification

Add deterministic upstream-clock, concurrency, lost-response, storage failure and revocation-race tests. Prove >32h simulated refresh cadence through seven days. In the HTTPS pilot prove the old downstream JWT has actually expired before using the renewed one. If shortening the pilot lifetime to exercise refresh, label that evidence separately from actual seven-day wall-clock verification.
